item.title: Find and Use Catalog Designs
item.description:
The catalog holds published designs: reusable infrastructure patterns that anyone can inspect and any signed-in user with the right permission can clone. This guide covers finding a design, using it, and managing the entries you own. For how the catalog works, who can publish, and what the metrics mean, see Catalog.

Before you start 🔗

  • Browsing needs no account. Signed-out visitors can search, filter, and read every published design.
  • Cloning, downloading, editing, and deleting need you to sign in and hold the matching permission. A role without the permission sees the action disabled. See Roles and Permissions.
  • Cloning needs an organization. The copy lands in your selected workspace, so you must have an organization selected. Cloud refuses a clone while the all-organizations view is active.
Action Permission Notes
Browse, search, read details None Open to signed-out visitors.
Open in the Playground None Changes there are never written back to the catalog design.
Clone Clone Design Source must be published or public.
Download Download a design Core YAML only, without catalog metadata.
Edit catalog details Publish Design Type, technology, description, and caveats.
Unpublish Unpublish Design You must be the design’s creator or hold Approve Catalog Request.
Delete Delete a design You must own the design. Provider administrators are the exception.

item.title: Catalog
item.description:
The catalog is the library of designs that their owners have published for everyone to use. It turns a design that worked for one team into a reusable starting point for every other team: anyone can find it, read it, and see how often others open, deploy, and clone it, and any signed-in user can clone it into their own workspace and adapt it.

The catalog works on a simple contract. Publishing makes a design readable by the world and clonable by any signed-in user, a review step decides what gets in, and a class label tells readers who stands behind each entry. The rest of this page explains each part of that contract and where it stops.
